sub_scenario.one_line: fraud response director: send the attack-path canvas and ask the deputy to lead tonight

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the attack-path canvas and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The fraud roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I make good daytime fraud-containment calls when the attack path is sketched.
What does the sketch show?
Which merchant, identity, and payout controls have to close first.
Someone new shadowed me in the response room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the after-hours escalations into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
In the vendor-token breach, I charted the path from credential reset to payout holds before freezing accounts.
What was the result?
We preserved legitimate merchants while stopping the fraudulent exit path.
I can review a normal afternoon loss report without strain.
Is that the same as an active fraud ring?
No. Reports do not force a live freeze decision.
I archived last cycle's notes on the fraud roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I have been awake through two 02:00 account-takeover escalations and have a recovery appointment tomorrow morning.
Why not take tonight too?
A third night would leave no recovery before the appointment.
A vendor call about the attack-path canvas ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the response room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the after-hours escalations.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the fraud roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On a prior uncharted takeover call, I froze payouts before closing the credential-reset route, and the attackers shifted channels.
What caused the miss?
I was making the chain up live after an overnight escalation.
I sketched next week's plan for the after-hours escalations before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the attack-path canvas updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My therapist and I set a no-night-call boundary during panic-symptom treatment; a written containment plan is the alternative.
Can you remain available asynchronously?
Yes. I can review the canvas before the room convenes.
I compared two options for the fraud roster tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the response room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Do I accept the 23:00 account-takeover war-room chair after two escalation nights?
